🌱 November 17, 2006 • The Seed That Started It All

Why I Funded the Desk—and Stepped Out of His Way.

When someone you love spends years being told their voice doesn’t matter, a pep talk isn’t enough. You get them out of that house, you hand them real tools with no strings attached, and you guard the perimeter while they remember who they are.

“I didn’t write a single chapter or melody on RaggieSoft—that’s 100% Michael. My pride is knowing the roof over his studio will never cave in.”
Read November 2006 in The Rachel NarrativeNext: Meet Bear & Bug →

Four Chapters from Delaney Street to Moosewood Drive

Select any era below to see how our three-sibling studio came together.

Virginia Beach, Virginia

Moving Christmas Up When Everything Was on the Line

I had secretly put together a dream portable studio workstation, music production suite, and design toolkit—double-boxed in plain cardboard—planning to surprise Michael at Christmas so he would see a future beyond his abuser’s roof. When Delores threw him out in mid-November, Christmas moved up that very night. We got him safe, unboxed the workstation, and backed him with the seed money to build on his own terms.

Jessica’s Takeaway: I provided the rescue and the seed money; every creative spark that followed was 100% Michael’s.
